Cross-validate a fitted hib mixed-effects model

Source: R/hib_cv_model.R
hib_cv_model.Rd

This function re-fits models on different subsets of the data, so that subsequent evaluation of model performance can take place.

Usage

hib_cv_model(
  mod_obj,
  db_obj,
  fold_type,
  custom_col = NULL,
  random_seed = NULL,
  re_form = list(NA),
  backtransform = NULL,
  use_original_mesh = NULL
)

Arguments

mod_obj

One of; HibModelLME4, HibModelINLA or HibModelBRMS.

db_obj

A HibDatabase object, or, if modelling used multiple data- sources, a list of database objects

fold_type

A character indicating the type of cross-validation; one of: "Random-2", "Random-3", "Random-5", "Random-10", "Source_ID", "SS", "Country", "UN_subregion", "UN_region", "Biome", "Realm", "Custom"

custom_col

A character indicating the column in the model data to use to define cross-validation folds, when fold_type == "Custom"

random_seed

A numeric indicating the random seed used to define random cross-validation folds - only used if 'Random-X' in fold_type

re_form

A list indicating the random effects variables to be included in the cross-validation/insample predicitons - if multiple items supplied, each option will be used in a separate cv prediction. Values can be either NA (no random effects), NULL (all random effects), or a rhs formula specifying particular random effects to include. Note: only test set data points with random-effect values present in the training data will have predictions if re_form is not NA.

backtransform

A function to convert the model prediction back to the original scale of interest

use_original_mesh

A logical value indicating whether cross-validation of spatial INLA models should use the original mesh for all cv folds. Computationally this is slightly more efficient, but may affect cv performance metrics - witheld sites will still exist in the mesh.

Details

Expects a HibModel.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  cv_out <- hib_mod_cv(mod_obj, db_obj, fold_type = "UN_region")
} # }
